reviewer: Codex main agent; lower-cost agents gathered context and retrieval evidence only
summary: Rejected on repeated one-time payoffs and concrete continuity/cost defects, including repeated editorial/book/spirits premises. All scoped cards and their first three non-self retrieval candidates were read in full.

issues.problem: The knowing pool describes one-time payoffs, but repeat: 1 permits another showing after a month. These 15 cards have fixed scenes and no completion gate. They can stage the same problem and resolution again, including with the same classmate when per: x is used.
issues.fix: Remove the cooldown from the shared pool through the project migration workflow for one-time payoffs. Give any intentionally recurring card a suitable cooldown and variation that accounts for prior outcomes.

issues.problem: The opening says Kael told the player the Northern goodbye custom once, but only met/relationship/month are required. A month-4 state with no kael_until_the_thaw showing and no kael.thaw knowledge passes the gate.
issues.fix: Gate the explicit recollection on the source scene/known fact, or use an unfamiliar-behaviour opening when that conversation has not happened.

issues.problem: The card finds a ward in courtyard snow and later hands it to Ilse beside Kael, yet there is no winter or Ilse-availability gate. It remains a candidate in spring after ilse_taken, when she cannot receive it.
issues.fix: Require the appropriate season and available named characters, or write separate season/absence outcomes that respect the existing story flags.

issues.problem: Mending deducts study -tiny, but the outcome describes careful needlework and the siblings recognizing their mother’s stitch without any missed academic work. It can also occur on a break without courses.
issues.fix: Name the revision/homework actually sacrificed and make it meaningful in the eligible window, or use a cost the mending shows.

issues.problem: Both a successful explanation and the chess route end with “Pay for the glass,” yet neither success path deducts gold or queues a payment. Only the failed explanation charges the purse.
issues.fix: Apply the promised glass payment on both success paths, or change the instruction/outcome so it does not promise an unimplemented payment.

issues.problem: This repeats nessa_between_story’s conflict: Nessa wants to print a nonconsensual account of a friend’s trouble, and the player intervenes to protect the friend. The known quill rule supplies another solution to the same editorial/privacy choice.
issues.fix: Add the known-fact solution to the existing card, or give this payoff a different interview conflict rather than another unwanted story about a friend.

issues.problem: This repeats nessa_fact_check: Nessa hands over proofs containing planted errors; the player searches them and earns editorial approval. The earlier card already includes finding the planted one first and then fixing the others.
issues.fix: Put the knowledge-dependent approach into the existing fact-check card, or use the planted-error knowledge in a genuinely different problem.

issues.problem: This repeats grimsbys_by_the_nose’s request for a particular book and its existing success variant where describing the book by smell finds it immediately. The essay deadline does not change that encounter’s obstacle, action or punchline.
issues.fix: Fold the deadline/knowledge variant into the existing book request, or make the smell knowledge solve a different kind of problem.

issues.problem: The fixed opening reaches Grimsby at closing time and the ordinary search ends at ten, but the event has no slot/time restriction. Its bookshop can deal it at noon with full timeFit.
issues.fix: Constrain delivery to the appropriate closing-time slot, or make the prose fit ordinary shop hours.

issues.problem: The stairs story is explicitly a prepared false account, and choosing it conceals the true injury cause while obtaining treatment. It costs Mood but no Alignment, despite the rule that deliberate dishonesty has moral weight.
issues.fix: Give choosing the known lie its Hollow movement, or make the alternative an honest refusal to discuss the cause.

issues.problem: This repeats tide_water_spirit_race’s two solutions and payoff: compete physically against cheating water spirits, or ask politely and be carried across as a raft while Marisol approves. A storm and boat replace the class swim without changing that decision.
issues.fix: Give the storm crossing a different conflict/solution, or add the knowledge payoff to the established spirit-race encounter.

issues.problem: The right outcome explicitly says Grimsby sells the player a lighthouse book and “You buy it,” but no gold changes. Mood is the only purse-independent cost.
issues.fix: Charge for the purchase or make it an explicit gift/declined offer.

issues.problem: Winning “Say the printer is lying” falsely discredits a printer who is telling the truth, but Hollow movement happens only on a failed check. Successful dishonesty for reputational gain carries none.
issues.fix: Apply the moral cost to choosing the deception regardless of check result, while retaining outcome-specific social consequences.

limitations: No source repairs or gameplay-frequency estimates. Knowledge-gated better outcomes are intentional (phase4-plan §2); they were not treated as ungated routine dominance.
